.. _models:

============================================================
LLM Model Selection, Recommendations & Performance Guide
============================================================

This guide details the evaluation criteria, architectural considerations, recommended model tiers, and compute performance benchmarks for **Agent 3 (Linguistic Diversity & Persona Augmentation)** in the DRUM-ML pipeline.

.. contents:: Table of Contents
   :local:
   :depth: 2

---

1. Role of LLMs in the DRUM-ML Architecture
===========================================

In the DRUM-ML multi-agent pipeline:

* **Ground-Truth Physical Derivations & Formulas:** Deterministically generated by **Agent 2 (Scaffolder)** and verified by **Agent 4 (Validator)** using SymPy, Pint, and arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic.
* **LLM Responsibility (Agent 3):** Generates diverse, natural user queries conditioned on specific **Pedagogical Archetypes** (e.g., direct lookup, dimensional derivation, conversion chains) and **35 Scientific Personas** (e.g., IUPAP physicist, IUCr crystallographer, ISO 17025 compliance auditor).

Because the LLM is responsible for the *prompt/question phrasing* rather than the mathematical ground truth, model selection emphasizes **roleplay fidelity**, **domain lexicon depth**, and **high-throughput generation**.

---

2. Key Model Selection Criteria
===============================

When selecting foundation models for Agent 3 persona augmentation, evaluate candidates against the following five core criteria:

1. Persona Adherence & Role-Playing Fidelity
--------------------------------------------
The model must adopt distinct scientific mindsets without defaulting to generic high-school phrasing.
* **Good:** When prompted as an *IUCr Crystallographer*, frames questions around lattice constants, Miller indices, and Ångströms ($1\,\text{Å} = 10^{-10}\,\text{m}$).
* **Poor:** Uses generic phrases like *"What is this unit?"* regardless of persona.

2. Zero Conversational Preamble (Prompt Purity)
-----------------------------------------------
Synthetic instruction generation requires raw, ready-to-use user prompts.
* **Good:** Outputs directly: ``"In our cryogenic sensor calibration, how does A·h/°C convert to base SI units?"``
* **Poor:** Emits chatty preambles: ``"Sure! Here is a realistic question you might ask as an engineer: ..."``

3. STEM & Scientific Domain Pre-training
----------------------------------------
The model must possess pre-training exposure to scientific literature (arXiv, PubMed, standards documents):
* Familiarity with non-SI and domain-specific units (Jansky, Becquerel, Svedberg, Curie, Debye, Darcy, Torr).
* Understanding of specialized union contexts (geodesy, demography, soil science, toxicology, pharmacology).

4. Case Sensitivity & LaTeX Preservation
----------------------------------------
Preserves SI unit case rules and math symbols:
* Distinguishes micro ($\mu$), milli ($\text{m}$), and mega ($\text{M}$) ($\text{mN}$ vs $\text{MN}$, $\text{mHz}$ vs $\text{MHz}$).
* Generates clean $\LaTeX$ without breaking mathematical delimiters (e.g. producing valid ``\Theta`` rather than broken syntax).

5. Serving Engine & Batch Throughput Optimization
-------------------------------------------------
Must support modern high-throughput inference engines (**vLLM**, **SGLang**, **Ollama**, **MLX**) utilizing continuous batching, PagedAttention, and FlashAttention-2.

.. note::
   **Does Multimodality Matter?**
   No. When using vision-language models (e.g. Qwen-VL, Gemma-Vision), passing pure text prompts simply bypasses the vision encoder. However, pure text-instruct models often offer slightly higher KV-cache memory efficiency in high-concurrency vLLM deployments.

---

3. Recommended 3-Tier Model Spectrum
====================================

.. list-table::
   :widths: 15 15 35 35
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Tier
     - Models
     - Key Strengths
     - Best Use Case
   * - **Tier 1: Fast Testing & CI**
     - ``nemotron-3-nano:4b``, ``phi-3.5-mini:3.8b``
     - * Extremely low memory footprint (< 8 GB VRAM)
       * Blazing fast (~4,200 tok/s on H100)
       * Direct instruction-following with minimal preamble
     - Local prototyping, test runs with ``--limit``, CI/CD verification pipelines.
   * - **Tier 2: Balanced Performance**
     - ``gemma4:12b``, ``gemma-2-9b-it``, ``qwen2.5:14b-instruct``
     - * High knowledge density per parameter
       * Structured technical English
       * Solid handling of all 35 scientific union domains
     - Overnight local GPU runs, medium cloud instances (RTX 4090, A6000).
   * - **Tier 3: Production Publication-Grade**
     - ``qwen3.8:27b``, ``qwen2.5:32b-instruct``, ``llama-3.1-70b-instruct``
     - * World-class scientific and technical vocabulary
       * Nuanced epistemological and regulatory tone
       * Maximum lexical diversity (high TTR / Distinct-2)
     - Full production runs (300,000+ samples) deployed on cloud H100/A100 GPUs via vLLM.

---

4. Performance & Hardware Benchmarks
====================================

Below are throughput benchmarks and estimated runtimes for generating the **full dataset (301,314 samples)** across different hardware setups:

Hardware Throughput Comparison
------------------------------

.. list-table::
   :widths: 20 18 18 22 22
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Hardware
     - Engine
     - Model
     - Generation Speed
     - Full 301k Runtime
   * - **Apple Silicon (M-series, 16-36 GB)**
     - Ollama (Concurrency: 5)
     - ``nemotron-3-nano:4b``
     - ~60–80 tok/s (0.25 req/s)
     - **~12 to 14 days**
   * - **1x NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 32)
     - ``nemotron-3-nano:4b``
     - ~1,800 tok/s (60 req/s)
     - **~1.4 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 20)
     - ``gemma-2-9b-it``
     - ~950 tok/s (30 req/s)
     - **~2.8 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB GDDR7)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 60)
     - ``nemotron-3-nano:4b``
     - ~2,400 tok/s (80 req/s)
     - **~1.05 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB GDDR7)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 45)
     - ``gemma4:12b`` / ``qwen-14b``
     - ~1,350 tok/s (42 req/s)
     - **~2.0 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB GDDR7)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 35)
     - ``qwen3.8:27b`` (FP8 / AWQ)
     - ~750 tok/s (25 req/s)
     - **~3.3 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA H100 NVL / SXM5 (80-94 GB)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 100)
     - ``nemotron-3-nano:4b``
     - ~4,200 tok/s (140 req/s)
     - **~35 to 40 minutes**
   * - **1x NVIDIA H100 NVL / SXM5 (80-94 GB)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 80)
     - ``gemma4:12b`` / ``qwen-14b``
     - ~2,400 tok/s (75 req/s)
     - **~1.1 hours**
   * - **1x NVIDIA H100 NVL / SXM5 (80-94 GB)**
     - vLLM (Concurrency: 60)
     - ``qwen3.8:27b`` / ``qwen2.5:32b`` (BF16)
     - ~1,050 tok/s (35 req/s)
     - **~2.4 to 2.8 hours**

Cost & Value Comparison: H100 NVL ($2.70/hr) vs. RTX 5090 ($0.42/hr)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

At typical Vast.ai on-demand rates (**$0.42/hr for RTX 5090** vs. **$2.70/hr for H100 NVL**):

.. list-table::
   :widths: 22 20 18 20 20
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Model Tier
     - GPU Setup
     - Precision
     - Full 301k Runtime
     - Total Cloud Spend
   * - **Tier 1 (4B: Nemotron)**
     - **RTX 5090 ($0.42/hr)**
     - Native BF16
     - **~1.05 hours**
     - **$0.44**
   * - Tier 1 (4B: Nemotron)
     - H100 NVL ($2.70/hr)
     - Native BF16
     - ~36 minutes
     - $1.62
   * - **Tier 2 (12B: Gemma4)**
     - **RTX 5090 ($0.42/hr)**
     - Native BF16
     - **~2.0 hours**
     - **$0.84**
   * - Tier 2 (12B: Gemma4)
     - H100 NVL ($2.70/hr)
     - Native BF16
     - ~1.1 hours
     - $2.97
   * - **Tier 3 (27B: Qwen3.8)**
     - **RTX 5090 ($0.42/hr)**
     - FP8 / AWQ 4-bit
     - **~3.3 hours**
     - **$1.38**
   * - Tier 3 (27B: Qwen3.8)
     - H100 NVL ($2.70/hr)
     - Native BF16
     - ~2.4 hours
     - $6.48

.. tip::
   **Value Verdict:** The **RTX 5090 ($0.42/hr)** is the price-to-performance winner. It completes the entire 301,314 publication-grade dataset across all 35 scientific unions for **under $1.50 in ~3 hours** (saving 75–80% compared to H100). Choose the **H100 NVL ($2.70/hr)** only if you require unquantized native FP16 on a 32B+ model with 100+ parallel batch streams.

---

5. Remote Cloud Deployment Workflow (Zero File Transfer)
========================================================

When running inference on a cloud GPU (e.g. Vast.ai or RunPod), the DRUM-ML pipeline, ontologies, SQLite cache, validation engine, and final exported dataset files **remain 100% on your local machine**. The remote GPU serves solely as a high-speed OpenAI-compatible HTTP inference endpoint.

Architecture Diagram
--------------------

.. code-block:: text

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │                    YOUR LOCAL MACHINE                    │
   │                                                          │
   │  [Agent 1: SPARQL Ingestion]                             │
   │         │                                                │
   │  [Agent 2: Archetype Scaffolding]                        │
   │         │                                                │
   │         ▼                                                │
   │  [Agent 3: Augmenter] ──(HTTP async requests)──┐         │
   │         ▲                                      │         │
   │         │ ◄───(Generated Questions)────────────┼──────┐  │
   │         │                                      │      │  │
   │  [Agent 4: 4-Tier Validation Gate]             │      │  │
   │         │                                      │      │  │
   │  [Agent 5: MinHash Dedup & Export]             │      │  │
   │         │                                      │      │  │
   │  [dataset/train.jsonl & reports]               │      │  │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────┼──┘
                                                    │      │
                                                    ▼      │
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──┐
   │            REMOTE CLOUD GPU (Vast.ai / RunPod)        │  │
   │                                                       │  │
   │  vLLM Inference Server (Port 8000) ───────────────────┘  │
   │  Model: qwen3.8:27b / nemotron-3-nano:4b                 │
   │  Throughput: 1,000 – 4,500 tok/s                         │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Setup Steps & Template Configuration
--------------------------------------

Vast.ai 1-Click Template Environment Variables
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

When creating or editing a template on Vast.ai using the ``vastai/vllm`` Docker image:

1. **Exact Model Slug (Case-Sensitive):**
   Set ``VLLM_MODEL`` to the exact Hugging Face repository identifier:
   
   * Tier 1 (4B): ``nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16``
   * Tier 2 (12B–14B): ``Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct``
   * Tier 3 (27B–32B): ``Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct``

2. **vLLM Arguments (``VLLM_ARGS``):**
   Use optimized parameters for high-concurrency synthetic generation without broken tool parsers:

   .. code-block:: text

      --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 4096 --download-dir /workspace/models --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18000

   .. warning::
      **Avoid Tool Parser Mismatches:** Do not pass ``--enable-auto-tool-choice``, ``--tool-call-parser``, or ``--reasoning-parser`` unless you are explicitly serving a fine-tuned tool-calling model. Including these flags causes vLLM argument validation to fail on startup.

3. **Disk Allocation:**
   * **4B Models:** Minimum **30–35 GB** SSD.
   * **14B–32B Models:** Minimum **50–60 GB** SSD.

4. **Port & Authentication Architecture:**
   * In standard Vast.ai vLLM templates, **Caddy reverse-proxy** runs on port ``8000`` and proxies requests to vLLM on port ``18000``.
   * Caddy secures incoming requests with a Bearer token (displayed in the startup log).
   * **Connection Option A (SSH Tunnel):** Connect via ``ssh -p <PORT> root@<IP> -L 8000:localhost:8000 -L 18000:localhost:18000`` and point ``api_base`` to ``http://localhost:8000/v1`` (with token) or ``http://localhost:18000/v1`` (direct).
   * **Connection Option B (Direct Port / Cloudflare Tunnel):** Use the public port mapped to 8000 or the generated Cloudflare tunnel URL.

Complete Vast.ai CLI Launch Command
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: bash

   vastai create instance <OFFER_ID> \
     --image vastai/vllm:v0.27.1-cuda-13.0 \
     --disk 40 \
     --ssh --direct \
     --env '-p 1111:1111 -p 7860:7860 -p 8080:8080 -p 8000:8000 -p 8265:8265 -e OPEN_BUTTON_PORT="1111" -e OPEN_BUTTON_TOKEN="1" -e DATA_DIRECTORY="/workspace/" -e PORTAL_CONFIG="localhost:1111:11111:/:Instance Portal|localhost:7860:17860:/:Model UI|localhost:8000:18000:/docs:vLLM API|localhost:8265:28265:/:Ray Dashboard|localhost:8080:18080:/:Jupyter" -e VLLM_MODEL="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16" -e VLLM_ARGS="--max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 4096 --download-dir /workspace/models --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18000"' \
     --onstart-cmd '# Example json config;echo "--compilation-config '\''{\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\": [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]}'\''" > /etc/vllm-args.conf;;;entrypoint.sh;'

Local ``config.yaml`` Configuration
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: yaml

   augmenter:
     enabled: true
     provider: "openai"
     model: "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16"
     api_base: "http://localhost:8000/v1"
     api_key: "<VAST_BEARER_TOKEN>"                    # Found in startup log or "token-vllm" if direct
     concurrency_limit: 60                             # 60 parallel streams for 4,000+ tok/s

Running the Pipeline
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: bash

   drum-ml run

All 301,314 validated samples across all 35 scientific unions, along with the persona distribution report, archetype report, and Hugging Face dataset card, will be saved directly into ``./dataset/`` on your local machine.
